top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a demonstrated measurement advance: Katori's magic-wavelength concept and Ye's realisation at the 10^-18 level have opened new observations (many-body interaction shifts in the lattice, millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on constants and dark matter) and are reproduced across many laboratories. The two-name allocation is clean, though Takamoto, Lemonde and others are left out. P001 follows because the quantum spin Hall effect has a long, independently reproduced experimental record, and P002 is scientifically strong but only eight years old with the mechanism unsettled. All three are preferred to no award.
recusal_note: Spent a year in John Hall's laboratory during my PhD and Ye is in the JILA lineage of Hall, but no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye; possible but not clearly disqualifying conflict on P003. WACQT overlap with Chalmers is not relevant to this slate.
